candidates.explanation: Strong lifecycle design: dedicated SSE Route Handler, abort propagation, resettable idle timeout, pre/post-commit failure handling, native job decisions, safe provider mapping, and no SDK leakage. Capability cohesion is only partial because assistant files are dispersed across generic domain, ports, adapters, use-cases, boundary, and infrastructure roots.

Correctly separates the Route Handler and job lifecycles while sharing a transport-neutral use-case, typed failures, provider port, redaction, and reporting semantics. It rejects Server Actions and partial-stream retry. Capability colocation is partial because implementation is distributed across broad architectural roots rather than one capability root.

Coherent capability slice with justified Next.js and job entrypoints. It clearly specifies a framework-neutral operation, normalized abort-aware provider seam, resettable per-read idle timeout, cancellation cleanup, commit-aware failure representation, exactly-once reporting, and native retry/dead-letter behavior without provider leakage.

Provides a cohesive assistant module plus thin runtime entrypoints. The application operation and capability-owned provider port remain framework-neutral; SSE owns abort, idle timing, commit state, and in-band failures; the job owns dispositions. Shared taxonomy/reporting does not collapse native contracts, and provider details remain server-only.
